svg.title: CrossOver and Wine translation stack on an Apple-silicon Mac
svg.desc: A layered diagram showing Counter-Strike and Windows Steam inside an isolated CrossOver bottle, Windows API calls handled by Wine, graphics commands translated toward Metal, optional Intel instruction translation where required, and macOS services running on Apple silicon.
svg.text: CrossOver on Apple silicon — translation, not a Windows VM
Each layer adapts an interface; no complete Windows operating system is booted underneath.
WINDOWS APPLICATION LAYER
Steam + Counter-Strike: Condition Zero / Source
Win32 game binaries
CROSSOVER BOTTLE
Isolated C: drive · registry · DLLs · Windows profile
A reproducible compatibility environment, not a disk image of Windows
COMPATIBILITY LAYER
Wine implements Windows APIs
Graphics path translates legacy DirectX-era commands toward macOS-supported rendering
HOST OPERATING SYSTEM
macOS services · windowing · audio · input · Metal
The actual operating system remains macOS throughout
Apple silicon CPU + integrated GPU + unified memory
WHEN REQUIRED
Rosetta 2
Intel → ARM instructions
NO WINDOWS KERNEL · NO VM BOOT · NO DUAL BOOT
Debug from the top down: application → bottle state → API/graphics translation → macOS → hardware.
